subject: [Lumos Health] Production p95/p99 spike following A/B model rollout
messages:
From: Jared Coleman <jared.coleman@lumoshealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Patel <sara.patel@lumoshealth.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2028 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Production p95/p99 spike after today

Hi Hannah / Lauren,

We started seeing a big degradation in user-facing latency this morning right after your team pushed the A variant in our A/B test (traffic split ~20% A / 80% B). p95 went from ~320ms to 1.8s and p99 is showing 5–7s on our end for many calls — this is causing timeouts inside our web UI.

Attached a short trace and the canary metrics we pulled from our side (canary-metrics-20280614.csv). The incident began around 15:10 PDT and correlates with the rollout event we see in your audit logs.

Can you confirm whether this variant uses the new KV-cache optimization and whether you rolled any quantization changes? We need an ETA for mitigation or rollback — impact is customer-visible.

Thanks,
Jared Coleman
Director, Platform Engineering
Lumos Health

Attachments: perf-sample-20280614.log, canary-metrics-20280614.csv

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2028 16:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Production p95/p99 spike after today

Team — forwarding Lumos. Jared reports p95/p99 spike aligned with our A/B rollout (A variant at 20%). Key asks:
- Confirm whether A variant applied new kernel selection/kv-cache changes today
- Share canary metrics and per-host tail latencies (canary bucket breakdown)
- Recommend immediate mitigation: rollback A to previous model or reduce traffic to 0%

Ben: please pull platform traces and the rollout event (audit id attached in HubSpot link). Marissa: can you own customer comms (ack + ETA)? Rishi / Lauren: FYI — this escalates to exec level if not resolved in 60m.

I am attaching the request-trace we pulled from the ingress logs.

— Hannah
Senior TPM, Redwood Inference

Attachments: request-trace-1686778921.txt

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2028 16:52:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production p95/p99 spike after today

On Fri, Jun 14, 2028 at 4:38 PM Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Team — forwarding Lumos. Jared reports p95/p99 spike aligned with our A/B rollout (A variant at 20%).

Quick update from infra: initial kernel-level telemetry shows increased tokenization pre-processing time for model-A + higher KV cache misses at sequence lengths >512; suspect regression in recent kernel selector tweak (v0.9.3 -> v0.9.4).

We are running targeted canary replays now comparing v0.9.3 vs v0.9.4 on identical traffic slice. If the replay reproduces the tail, recommend immediate rollback of A to v0.9.3 and cut traffic on the experiment.

I'll paste replay results when ready (estimating 25–30m).

— Ben
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Coleman <jared.coleman@lumoshealth.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2028 17:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production p95/p99 spike after today

Hi Jared — thank you for the data and the heads up. We are treating this with highest priority. Current plan:
1) Run immediate canary replay (in progress) to validate the regression path (Ben owns).
2) If replay confirms regression, we will roll A back to v0.9.3 and revert experiment traffic to 0%.
3) We will provide a short post-incident note explaining root cause and next steps.

ETA: 45–60 minutes for first mitigation (rollback if confirmed). We will update you at the 30-minute mark. Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts your users.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success — Hosted Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Jared Coleman <jared.coleman@lumoshealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Jun 2028 17:29:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production p95/p99 spike after today

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Please confirm the rollback ETA and if you expect any data/state changes for our ongoing requests. Also — can you confirm if timeouts will cascade to downstream services? We saw several 502s last hour.

Thanks,
Jared

On Fri, Jun 14, 2028 at 5:10 PM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi Jared — thank you for the data and the heads up. We are treating this with highest priority...

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 15 Jun 2028 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production p95/p99 spike after today — rollback complete

Update: rollback of A variant to v0.9.3 completed at 09:02 PDT. Post-rollback telemetry: p95 returned to ~340ms, p99 back to ~1.1s within ~4 minutes. No user-facing data/state loss reported; ongoing requests that timed out will need retry from client side.

Actions next:
- Incident postmortem ticket created: HL-8721-INC-01 (initial notes in HubSpot).
- Root cause: kernel-selector change in v0.9.4 causing KV-cache inflation at long sequences; engineering will produce patch and will gate rollout behind additional canary criteria.
- CS follow-up: Marissa to send customer post-incident note and credit proposal.

— Rishi
VP, Serving Runtime

Attachments: post-rollback-metrics-20280615.csv
